title.narrative: Improving agricultural practices in Kenya with satellite soil health monitoring

description.narrative: Spatialise B.V. has developed a soil health monitor that uses satellite data and artificial intelligence to accurately analyse the nutrients in the topsoil of agricultural lands. This results in significant cost and time savings compared to traditional methods (manually collecting multiple soil samples per plot and taking them to the lab for analysis). The accurate data allows farmers to optimise their use of water, pesticides and fertilisers, leading to less waste and a lower environmental impact.In addition, it is a scalable (analysing large agricultural lands) and affordable solution for many large and medium-sized farmers, with a cost of only €2.00 per hectare per year.Kenya has a rapidly growing agricultural sector characterised by mainly open farming (for crops such as avocado, maize, pineapple, sorghum, sugar cane and wheat). The sector faces challenges such as irregular rainfall, soil erosion and the need for improved agricultural practices to increase yields. Especially in the crops mentioned above, where precision farming can play a major role in optimising yields, improving crop quality and making land use more sustainable,Spatialise's technology can be valuable. It will enable farmers to accurately and cost-efficiently analyse their soil health without the need for physical soil sampling.
